comments.author: clusterfoo
comments.story_title: What Would You Recommend to a Bright 14 Year Old?
comments.why_zh: Harvard 的 justice 课程，每个人都该看
comments.quote_zh: 有两个我总在推荐的讲座系列，我觉得每个人都该看
comments.text_zh: 要精通 genetics / molecular biology！如果我有时间完成学业，我会双修 biology / math 或 CS。天啊，等那个孩子 30 岁时，那得是多强的组合。感觉 biotech 就处在 computing 在 1930 年代所处的位置……接下来会发生什么，以及它将如何改变世界，既令人恐惧又令人兴奋。在“软”的一面（不管那是什么意思）：伦理学、伦理学的历史，从各种视角来看。有两个我总在推荐的讲座系列，我觉得每个人都该拿枪顶着自己脑袋去看（正如讲师本人所说）：- [VIDEO]——Harvard 关于 justice / ethics 的课程。- [LINK]——Robert Saposky（及嘉宾）讲人类行为的生物学。文学理论。更深入地理解象征、语言和创造力的大师们如何思考、如何组织他们的作品；文学史；等等，会为你打开新的思考方式，就像学习纯数学或编程一样。现在就差发明一台时间机器，把这番建议给我自己了！天哪，我当年真用得上它。
comments.text: Be well versed in genetics / molecular biology! - If I had the time to finish school, I'd double in biology / math or CS. Man will that be a killer combo when that kid is 30. It feels like biotech is where computing was in the 1930's... what's to come, and how it will change the world is both frightening and exciting. On the "soft" side (whatever that means): ethics, the history of ethics, from every point of view. Two lecture series I always recommend, and feel like everyone should watch with a gun to their head (as the instructor himself says): - [VIDEO] -- Harvard course on justice / ethics. - [LINK] -- Robert Saposky (and guests) on the biology of human behavior. Literary theory. Gaining a deeper understanding of how masters of symbolism, language, and creativity think and put together their work; the history of literature; etc. will open you up to new ways of thinking just like studying pure maths or programming would. Now to invent a time machine and give myself this advice! Boy I could've used it.

comments.why_zh: 关于 Trolley Problem 和道德推理的讲座，既有启发又有趣
comments.quote_zh: 这个 Harvard 关于 Justice 的讲座（The Moral Side of Murder）很有启发，而且看起来意外地有趣
comments.text_zh: 不幸的是，目前还没有人真正能完整阐明人类的全部价值观，尤其是因为它们在现实情境中常常相互冲突。哪些价值应该优先于其他价值？不同文化之间，以及每种文化内部不同人类群体之间的价值观差异，又该怎么办？你可能听说过 Trolley Problem。它有许多变体，而且还有更复杂的版本。这个 Harvard 关于 Justice 的讲座（The Moral Side of Murder）很有启发，而且看起来意外地有趣：[VIDEO] AGI 的问题比大多数其他技术更尖锐，因为它是基于软件的，这使其几乎不可能被有效监管，尤其是在全球范围内。
comments.text: Unfortunately, no one can really articulate the full set of human values yet, especially since they are often in conflict in real-world situations. Which value(s) should be prioritized over others? How about differing values between cultures and human groups within each culture? You might have heard of the Trolley Problem. There are many and more complicated variations of that. This Harvard session on Justice (The Moral Side of Murder) is edifying and surprisingly fun to watch: [VIDEO] The problem with AGI is more acute than most other technologies because it is software-based, which makes it nigh impossible to regulate effectively, especially globally.

comments.text_zh: 当然，从说服的角度我同意。但从“试着理解另一个人”的角度，我建议你读读维基百科上关于伦理学的页面 [1]。就我自己在这个话题上受过的教育：大学里的一门课（我读的是商科），以及看了一些哈佛大学的伦理学讲座 [0]。在我看来，伦理学课程教人获得更精细的词汇，用来解释自己的立场、理解别人的立场。原评论者（GP）在这件事上显然采用的是义务论的思路。他/她认为“不人道、野蛮”的东西，唤起的是这样一种思路：他认为人不该做某种行为，因为这本身就是错的。我并不擅长解释义务论伦理学，持这种想法的人也不擅长。我的意思是：GP 所说的那类陈述背后有大量思考，我认为值得想一想。[0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]
comments.text: Sure, from a persuasion point of view I agree. But from a "trying to understand another human" point of view, I'd recommend you to read the Wikipedia page on ethics [1]. My own education on the topic: a course in college (as a business student) and watching some of the Harvard lectures on ethics [0]. IMO ethics courses teaches people to gain a more fine-grained vocabulary on explaining their own positions and understanding other's positions. GP clearly uses a deontological line of thinking on this matter. Something that GP considers to be "inhuman and barbaric" invokes a line of thinking in where he/she believes one ought to not do a certain action, because it simply is wrong. I'm not the best at explaining deontological ethics, nor are the people who think like this. My point is: a lot of thought has gone into the types of statements that GP makes, and IMO it's worth thinking about. [0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]

comments.author: jasonhong
comments.story_title: I am rich and have no idea what to do
comments.text_zh: 我和楼主（OP）的处境有些相似：多年前有过一次成功的退出，然后一直在琢磨接下来该做什么。我很幸运，当时还保有一所顶尖大学的教职，有年幼的孩子，也有一个很好的家庭帮我稳住脚跟、给我指引。我对这件事的总体看法是：在这个世界上，金钱是我们最接近超能力的东西之一。有了足够的钱，你可以建造新东西，朝着解决难题迈出步子，并影响人和组织去做你想做的事。既然如此，你想生活在一个什么样的世界里？借助你新获得的这种超能力，你能采取哪些步骤，让我们更接近那个世界？当然，这条路充满许多挑战和危险（尤其是看看世界各地那么多拥有超能力的亿万富翁，他们想让我们生活在寡头统治之下，不过那是改天再发的牢骚了）。最后，我想分享几样帮助塑造了我思考的东西——关于我如何花时间，以及我想对世界产生什么样的积极影响：- [LINK] - 约翰·罗尔斯（John Rawls）论无知之幕与原初立场 [LINK] - 迈克尔·桑德尔（Michael Sandel）教授（哈佛）论正义：何为正当之事？[VIDEO] - 罗伯特·赖希（Robert Reich）教授关于财富与贫困的课程（美国前劳工部长）[LINK] 还有一篇对一位科幻作家的采访（我相信是 Ted Chiang，但我找不到原文来确认），也提出了一个有趣的问题：你理想的世界是什么，而哪一步
comments.text: I was in a somewhat similar position as the OP, having had a successful exit many years ago and trying to figure things out. I was lucky that I still had a faculty position at a top university, young kids, and a good family to help ground me and guide me. My general take on things is this: money is one of the closest things we have to a superpower in this world. With enough money, you can build new things, make steps toward solving hard problems, and influence people and organizations to do things you want. Given all this, what kind of world would you want to live in? And with your newfound superpower, what kind of steps can you take that might get us closer to that world? Now, of course, this path is fraught with many challenges and dangers (especially as evidenced by so many superpowered billionaires around the world that want us to live in an oligarchy, but that's a rant for another day). Instead, I'll end by sharing a few things that have helped shape my thinking about how I spend my time and what kind of positive impact I want to make on the world: - [LINK] - John Rawls on the Veil of Ignorance and the original position [LINK] - Prof. Michael Sandel (Harvard) on Justice: What's the Right Thing to do?
